editorial:
Imagine finding a list of songs the Beatles never actually wrote and deciding to finish the job yourself. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow Rastko Ćirić and Goran Skrobonja, two creative guys from Belgrade who are obsessed with the Fab Four. They aren't just fans; they are artists and writers who want to capture that specific magic from the 1960s. The vibe is light and curious, feeling less like a stiff history lesson and more like a passion project between best friends. You will see them dive deep into the songwriting process, trying to figure out how the Beatles thought and felt while they were recording their most famous hits.

What really makes this work is the genuine love for music. You will love seeing the band come together to record the album, though the pacing can feel a bit slow in the middle since it is a documentary. It is a great pick if you love music history or just like seeing people chase a wild dream.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing the final result of their hard work: the completed album. You see the band performing the songs they wrote based on those lost titles. It ends on a happy note, proving that they successfully captured the spirit of the Beatles. There is no big twist, just the satisfying feeling of seeing a creative experiment actually work out and become a real piece of music.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music history and the Beatles.
